card.title: Allow Each Value At Most Twice

a1.cap: nums is sorted. Remove extra copies in place so every value appears at most twice, keeping the order. Return k, the new length; the first k slots of nums must hold the result.

lines: nums is sorted. Remove extra copies in place so every value appears at most twice, keeping the order. Return k, the new length; the first k slots of nums must hold the result.

a1.cap: For example, with nums = [1,1,1,2,2,3], the answer is [1,1,2,2,3].
a1.say: For example, with nums equals 1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, the answer is 1, 1, 2, 2, 3.

a1.cap: Keep a write pointer W. A value may be written if fewer than two values are written so far, or if it differs from the value two slots behind W.
That single comparison guarantees no value appears three times in a row.
Let's walk through it with nums = [1,1,1,2,2,3].
a1.say: Let's walk through it with nums equals 1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3.

a1.cap: 1 is allowed, so write it at index 0.
1 is allowed, so write it at index 1.
2 is allowed, so write it at index 2.
2 is allowed, so write it at index 3.
3 is allowed, so write it at index 4.
The answer is the first 5 slots.
Time complexity is O(n) and extra space is O(1).
a1.say: Time complexity is O of n and extra space is O of one.

a1.cap: That's the Two Pointers (read & write) approach. Now try writing it yourself, in Java or Python!
